# Barrel generation

Read when a package's generated `src/index.ts` barrel, its `exportsGeneration` option, or the ctix invocation behind them is in question. This page holds the whole rule; `SKILL.md` keeps only the index line.

## Barrels are generated by the build, not in front of it

`getTsdownConfiguration` runs ctix from a `build:prepare` hook, so no manifest repeats the command. What a package generates is the `exportsGeneration` option — `"typescript"` by default, `"vue"` for the package that ships components, `"none"` for one that names its own entrypoints and would otherwise get a barrel nothing is an entry for. `export:gen` still regenerates a barrel without a build — a typecheck needs the barrel and nothing else the build produces — but it runs the same function through the `generate-exports` bin `@esposter/configuration` declares, so a manifest names the bin and passes the answer, never a ctix config path. That bin is a committed `bin/generateExports.js` importing `../dist/index.js`, because pnpm refuses to link a shim whose target is missing at install time and `dist` is gitignored. `@esposter/configuration` itself spells the script `node bin/generateExports.js`: pnpm links a package's bins for its dependents, never for itself. `ctix` is a devDependency of `@esposter/configuration` alone, resolved from there rather than found on `PATH`.

Two things make it work, and both look redundant until they are gone:

- **`entry` is stated even though it is tsdown's own default.** Left unset, tsdown treats the default as a glob and resolves it _while resolving the config_, before any hook runs — so a package whose barrel is not on disk dies with `No input files`, which is every fresh clone. A literal entry reaches rolldown, which reads it after `build:prepare`.
- **The option is a union of literals, never an enum.** `packages/configuration` reaches its own source through `#src/*`, and tsdown loads a config with Node's strip-only type stripping: an enum fails outright with `TypeScript enum is not supported in strip-only mode`. A type erases to nothing.

Generation is **unguarded** — ctix runs on every build. A barrel of `export * from` names no symbol, so it reads as a function of the source file list and nothing else, which is what makes a hash-and-skip guard look obvious. It is not one, and the reason is worth knowing on its own: ctix resolves two files exporting the same identifier by **dropping both from the barrel**, printing a `detect same name of export statement` warning and exiting 0 — a case-conflicting filename is its only non-zero exit. So a rename that creates a collision changes what ctix writes while moving no path and adding no file, and no cheap key can see it. It is also the one way a package loses a public export with every check green: `publint`, `attw`, `deps.onlyImport` and typecheck all pass, because none of them knows what the barrel _should_ have held, and the warning scrolls past inside a whole-workspace build. What prevents that is the naming convention rather than a check — one export per file, named after the file (`file-organization`, `naming`) — and don't add a guard over the barrel to catch it either, because asserting over generated output fails on a fresh clone instead of on the regression (`testing`). What makes the absent skip cost nothing is the `package-builds` cache, which restores `dist` and the barrels together on an exact content hash; a build that misses it is regenerating every package regardless.
